newsitem.title: USA: Fuisz Technologies buys Irish drug maker.
newsitem.headline: Fuisz Technologies buys Irish drug maker.

text.p: Fuisz Technologies Ltd said Tuesday it had signed definitive agreements with the Cross Group to acquire a subsidiary that makes drugs in Ireland.
Fuisz said in a statement it will issue 1.0 million common shares to the owners of Clonmel Healthcare Ltd and pay $12.5 million in the form of non-interest bearing notes.
It said the owners have agreed to retain the shares for at least 12 months and retain at least 50 percent for a further 12 months.
It also said it will give the notes in three installments due in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
Clonmel's revenues totalled $19.4 million for the 12 months ended June 30, it added.

"The acquisition of Clonmel Healthcare represents an important step in our overall strategy to establish a major manufacturing presence in Ireland to supply our increasing clientele for Fuisz products both in Europe and the (United States)," it said.
Fuisz Technologies makes the capsules, chewable tablets and other formats for pharmaceutical companies to use to package their drugs.
A spokesman for the company said Fuisz was planning to eventually make its own drugs with the acquisition of Clonmel.
